result:
The proposed answer of 34 is not supported, so I reject it.

The solution gives a valid lower bound of 25, from R(K₅, K₄) = 25, and a loose upper bound from R(5,5). It then jumps to 34 by citing "edge-counting arguments with computer-assisted verification", with no actual derivation. The known values it lists (R(K₄, K₅−e) = 22 and R(K₄, K₅) = 25) do not lead to 34.

From memory, the best known results put R(K₅−e, K₅) near the low end of the range, around 25 to 27. I could not recall or verify the exact value, so I am not relying on it. Even so, 34 is implausibly high given that R(K₅−e, K₅−e) = 22.

VERDICT: REJECT
